title: £3.6 Million Bridging Loan
h1: Not revealed by search snippets. The search-result title of the page is "£3.6 Million Bridging Loan" (seen identically in [a] and [b]); the slug adds "prime Kensington property".
summary: Case study of a £3.6 million bridging facility arranged by Silver Oak Capital on a high-value (prime) residential property in Kensington, London. Purpose: refinance an existing debt/loan and raise additional capital for future acquisitions/purchases. Challenge: two specialist lenders had withdrawn at the final stage over intercreditor disagreements about first and second charges, leaving the borrower under time pressure. Structure/solution: Silver Oak worked with one lender to secure a single first-charge bridging loan that repaid the existing debt and covered the full capital raise, so no second charge was needed. Pricing stated on the page: 0.78% per month, BBR-linked (Bank of England base rate). Timing: completed within four weeks. The case study page does not name the lender (search summary refers to the page's "trusted lender" wording); a trade publication (Bridging & Commercial) reported the same transaction in October 2024 as completed by Octane Capital, originated by BDM Lee Warne and introduced by broker Jimmy Baillie of Silver Oak Capital. Borrower type is not described beyond 'the borrower' (owner of a high-value Kensington home seeking refinance and capital raise). Property value, LTV, loan term and exit strategy are not revealed in the results.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.content: Two specialist lenders had previously withdrawn / pulled out at the final stage due to disagreements over intercreditor terms relating to first and second charges, which left the borrower under time pressure.

sections.heading: The solution / structure
sections.content: Silver Oak worked with one lender to secure a first-charge bridging loan that repaid the existing debt and covered the full capital raise, without a second charge. The case study does not name the lender; the search summary says the page uses "trusted lender" wording.

sections.heading: Outcome / terms
sections.content: Completed within four weeks, priced at 0.78% per month, BBR-linked. [b] notes the page is about 230 days old (relative to 2026-10-29), so the terms are historical and not current quotes.

sections.heading: External corroboration (not on the Silver Oak page)
sections.content: Bridging & Commercial headline: "Octane Capital has completed £3.6m bridging loan secured against a Kensington house in four weeks." The search summary says the trade publication reported the transaction in October 2024 as completed by Octane Capital, with the loan originated by BDM Lee Warne and introduced by broker Jimmy Baillie from Silver Oak Capital. A separate Bridging & Commercial result is titled "Silver Oak Capital completes its largest ever bridging loan of £19.1m" (firm-level, different deal). A FIBA result is titled "Octane Capital completes £4m bridging loan on Kensington residential property"; [b] says the case studies index lists a separate £4 million Kensington bridging case study, but the results do not explicitly connect the two.

sections.heading: Related site-wide context surfaced by [b]
sections.content: General bridging page (/bridging-loans-uk/): bridging loans are typically issued for 12 to 24 months and are assessed mainly on property value, exit strategy and deal viability rather than income. Types-of-borrowing page: illustrative example of a £12 million loan at 0.75% per month over 12 months, with 2.00% lender fees and no exit fee. A page not in the seed surfaced: /bridging-loans-for-prime-central-london-purchases/ titled "Bridging Loans in the UK for Prime Central London Purchases".
